summary: P0 root-only admin lockdown VERIFIED end-to-end. Backend: 9/9 pytest cases pass against public URL — regular user and non-root admin (admin@test.com) both get 403 on /api/admin/setup, /promote, /demote; root super-admin (veales.vedic.decisions@gmail.com) successfully promotes a fresh user to admin (200), GET /api/admin/users reflects the change, then demotes (200), and the user disappears from /api/admin/users; root cannot demote self (got 400 'Cannot demote yourself'); /api/admin/users regression for non-root admin still returns 200 with admin list. Frontend (mobile viewport 375x667, logged in as harden_1777921741@example.com): Profile page has ZERO 'Administration' header occurrences, ZERO 'Become Super Admin'/'Manage Admins' UI, ZERO Super/Co-Admin/Admin role badges in header, ZERO admin quick links from the gated list (Authorized Experts, Decision Templates, Central Catalog, ReviewNet, Tier Matrix, Customer Segments, Org Members, Pending Approvals, Admin Settings, Documentation Hub, Decision Modes, Incident Response, Social Learning, WOWO ACM). Account Security section IS visible (shows 'Password Set' + 'Change' button). ScrollView correctly has flex:1 — inner scrollable measured scrollHeight=2077 / clientHeight=603 and scrolls smoothly via wheel + programmatic scrollTop; bottom of page (Logout + footer) reached successfully.

minor.issue: Root demote-self returns 400 'Cannot demote yourself' instead of the 403 'Root super-admin cannot be demoted' that the spec line indicates. Functionally still safe (root never gets demoted) because the 'Cannot demote yourself' check fires first at line 344 before the root-email check at line 347. Consider reordering so the explicit root-protection rule wins, for clearer security semantics.

action_items: (Optional) In /app/backend/routes/decisions.py demote_user(), move the ROOT_SUPER_ADMIN_EMAIL guard ABOVE the 'Cannot demote yourself' check so root demote-self yields 403 with the root-specific message rather than 400 (clearer security semantics; not blocking).
critical_code_review_comments: core/auth.py: require_root_super_admin enforces BOTH email match AND role==super_admin — correctly closes the self-elevation hole.
routes/decisions.py /admin/setup also re-checks email == ROOT_SUPER_ADMIN_EMAIL (defense in depth) — good.
profile.tsx (1439 lines) is over the 700-line guideline; consider splitting admin-section quick links into a separate component file in a future iteration. Not blocking this fix.
All 14 admin quick links named in the spec are properly gated behind {userRole !== 'user' && (...)} blocks; confirmed by runtime check (zero leaked to the regular user).
seed_data_creation: Per test run, registers an ephemeral target_<timestamp>@example.com user to receive the positive-path promote/demote. The test ends with that account demoted back to regular user, so it leaves the admin set unchanged.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend admin lockdown tests live at /app/backend/tests/test_root_admin_lockdown.py and run against EXPO_BACKEND_URL (default https://repo-blueprint-1.preview.emergentagent.com). Re-use them for any future regression of admin RBAC. Did NOT run scripts/revoke_unauthorized_admins.py — main agent explicitly forbade it because admin@test.com is needed for negative-path tests.
rca_of_issue: Original P0: any authenticated user could call POST /api/admin/setup and self-promote to super_admin, then call /promote on anyone. Fix landed in two layers: (1) /api/admin/setup now re-validates email == ROOT_SUPER_ADMIN_EMAIL (hard-coded constant in core/auth.py, env-overridable but never API-mutable); (2) /api/admin/promote and /api/admin/demote now depend on require_root_super_admin which requires BOTH the hard-coded email AND role==super_admin. Verified: no other account — including the existing admin@test.com (role=admin) — can mutate roles. Frontend layer additionally hides every role-management UI from non-admins, so the attack surface is gone from both client and server.
